In Canada you do have other options that require no licensing to transport or operate. It's perfectly legal to own a crossbow provided it can't be fired with one hand, and it exceeds half a meter in length. A crossbow with a 185 - 200 lbs draw is extremely accurate and lethal to a range of approximately 100 meters. A compound bow has even fewer restrictions and is lethal at a range of 30 to 60 meters depending on draw weight. With broadhead tips and high quality shafts these weapons can bring down anything from a 70 Kg deer to a 330 Kg elk.

A reasonably good crossbow with a decent scope goes for about $450 - $500 CAD. The PSE Fang is a really good starter kit with a 155 lbs draw and a 4x scope that will send bolts out at 105 meters per second and is lethal to about 70 meters with best stopping power peaking at about 30 meters. You're not going to hunt bear with it (you want 200lbs or more draw for that) but it's perfect for deer hunting.

Bows will never live up to the performance of a good rifle, but they should not be underestimated.

Filter I made to fit in my funnel for homebrewing

I had to use multiple small pieces because the scrap cloth I had wasn't big enough. I needed a cone with a 15cm diameter base and a 13cm long side. My calculations indicated that a 200° section of a 13cm radius circle would make the right size cone. And it did!

I included about 1cm seam allowance on each edge of the cloth wedges, and padded the measurements for insurance, so it was a bit of a fly by night operation but it worked out. I'm happy.

I didn't hem the wide end of the cone- I might add a cylindrical extension for handling or squishing when the filter is full.
